{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#cor-hoeffding-two-sided}
#### Hoeffding's inequality, two-sided

Under the assumptions of @thm-hoeffding, for every $\tolout > 0$,

$$
\Prf{\abs{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean} \ge \tolout} \le 2e^{-2n\tolout^2}.
$$ {#eq-hoeffding}

:::

::: proof

The variables $1 - X_1, \ldots, 1 - X_n$ are IID, lie in $[0, 1]$, and have mean $1 - \mean$.
Their sample mean is $1 - \samplemean{X}{n}$,
so @thm-hoeffding applied to them gives

$$
\ba
\Prf{\mean - \samplemean{X}{n} \ge \tolout}
&= \Prf{(1 - \samplemean{X}{n}) - (1 - \mean) \ge \tolout}
&& \text{(rearrange the event)} \\
&\le e^{-2n\tolout^2}
&& \text{(Hoeffding's inequality for } 1 - X_i \text{)}
\ea
$$

The event $\set{\abs{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean} \ge \tolout}$ is the union of $\set{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean \ge \tolout}$ and $\set{\mean - \samplemean{X}{n} \ge \tolout}$.
The probability of a union is at most the sum of the probabilities,
so

$$
\ba
\Prf{\abs{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean} \ge \tolout}
&\le \Prf{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean \ge \tolout} + \Prf{\mean - \samplemean{X}{n} \ge \tolout}
&& \text{(union bound)} \\
&\le e^{-2n\tolout^2} + e^{-2n\tolout^2}
&& \text{(Hoeffding's inequality, twice)} \\
&= 2e^{-2n\tolout^2}
&& \text{(combine like terms)}
\ea
$$

:::
